sections.heading: What is ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint?

blocks.text: **ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint** is a compile-time TypeScript concept that erases at emit — the run-time behavior is still JavaScript. sections.heading: Why ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint matters in production

blocks.text: Senior interviews and on-call debugging both test **ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint** beyond one-line definitions. Production failures here look like silent data corruption, memory growth, type errors at CI, or async ordering bugs — not syntax errors. Pitfalls for ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint
blocks.body: Treating ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint as pure syntax without compile-time or run-time behavior. Skipping validation at API/JSON boundaries. Ignoring strict compiler flags differences. Hand-waving in design review without a test or metric.

blocks.text: Prove mastery of **ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint** with a failing test that captures the edge case, a DevTools or heap snapshot showing the bug, and a clear tradeoff statement in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the compiler and emitted JS actually do — plus when the simple explicit version beats the clever abstraction.

blocks.title: What fails senior loops
blocks.body: Cannot trace a production bug to ESLint type-aware rules and @typescript-eslint. Says "it just works" without naming run-time checks, error paths, or JavaScript and C# differences.
